column1: # Contrast sets for the Particles game: four sentences that differ by one small word, each with its meaning.
好 · 好吗 · 好吧 · 好啊
column10: One word, four moods: the particle at the end carries the tone.

column1: 了 · 在 · 不 · 没
column7: I won't eat it / I don't eat that.
column9: I didn't eat / I haven't eaten.
column10: 了 = done · 在 = in the middle of it · 不 = won't / don't · 没 = didn't.

column8: 他 要 来 了 。
column10: 要…了 = about to happen. 不 talks about intentions, 没 about what (didn't) happen.
吗 asks, 吧 suggests, 也 adds "too". A bare 你去 sounds like an order.

column4: 你 饿 了 吧 ？
column5: You must be hungry by now, right?
column10: 了 adds "by now" (the state changed); 吧 turns it into a guess.
又…了 = again (already happened) · 还在 = still going on.
啦 = 了 + 啊: the same news, warmer.

column8: 你 懂 了 吗 ？
column10: 懂了 = the moment it clicks; 懂 alone is a steady state.

column2: 你 是 老师 吗 ？
column4: 你 是 老师 吧 ？
column10: 吗 = neutral question · 吧 = you're guessing · no particle + rising voice = surprise.

column5: No, I don't have one / I didn't.
column10: Chinese has no single word for "no": you negate the verb that was asked about.

column1: 好 了 · 好的 · 好啦 · 还好
column6: 好 啦 好 啦 。
column10: Four everyday "OK"s that mean very different things.
Same pattern as 好: the particle sets the tone.
